QUESTION OF THE WEEK - Given that most market players see second quarter inflation and wages data due on July 23 and 24 respectively as the key to a fifth interest rate cut, economists were surveyed on their expectations.

Generally, the data is expected to be favourable to interest rate bulls. The CPI is expected to be close to flat in the quarter, and well under 1.0 percent for the year, as the impact of lower interest rates continues to feed through.
Underlying inflation, which the Reserve Bank targets, is expected to fall out of the bottom of the two to three percent target range for the first time since the March 1995 quarter.
If the underlying rate falls below 1.8 percent in annual terms, it will be the lowest annual rate since March 1972, when the series began.

And wages are not expected to present any obstacle to an easing, with the highest quarterly forecast for average weekly ordinary time earnings annualising to a rate of four percent, under the RBA's 4.5 percent speed limit. ----------------------------------------------------------------
